author: Joe Fitzgerald Rodriguez
title: The San Francisco Standard
text:
A raucous and, occasionally, ill-tempered meeting of the San Francisco Democratic Party Wednesday night featured impassioned pleas, angry interruptions and a five-minute recess as members weighed whether to endorse District 8 supervisor candidate Manny Yekutiel.
At the center of it all was an allegation of sexual assault.
Two months ago, a political organizer accused San Francisco supervisor candidate Manny Yekutiel of forcibly grabbing his testicles and attempting to penetrate him with his fingers at a 2020 house party. Yekutiel denied the claims.
Wednesday evening, the Democratic Party endorsed him.
After three rounds of voting, members of the San Francisco Democratic Party board voted to solely endorse Yekutiel in the District 8 supervisors race to represent the Castro, Noe Valley and other neighborhoods.
After two rounds of voting in which no District 8 candidate won a majority, including Yekutiel, Rep. Nancy Pelosi aide Gary McCoy, marketing strategist Darshini Patel, nor attorney Michael Nguyen, a single member changed their vote, allowing Yekutiel to earn the endorsement: Supervisor Matt Dorsey, who initially backed McCoy before switching to Yekutiel.
“I know Gary very well. He’s someone I consider a friend. He’s someone I consider a colleague,” Dorsey said, saying McCoy’s journey in drug recovery would bring needed representation to the Board of Supervisors.
The multiple votes followed a ranked choice process that eliminates candidates each round if they fail to get a majority. During the third vote, Democratic Party board members could only decide between Yekutiel and “no endorsement.”
After they cast their vote, members of the crowd shouted “gross,” “disgusting” and Chapin said “shame on you.”
After the vote, and the jeers, multiple party board members asked for clarification of the process, seemingly confused at how it works.
The chair of the party, Nancy Tung, tried to explain the process using an example of apples, oranges, bananas, lychee and grapes.
“Who didn’t vote for lychee in the first round? I don’t know!” she said.
Hours before the meeting, a judicial commission working at the behest of the Democratic Party released its findings earlier that day, and concluding it could not recommend action against Yekutiel in response to Chapin’s claims because it lacked jurisdiction since the alleged assault did not occur at “an official meeting or any sponsored event of the [SF Democratic Party].”
But before a single vote was cast, Brad Joseph Chapin stood up and shamed the Democratic Party for asking him to recount the alleged assault despite knowing its own rules barred it from finding Yekutiel at fault.
“I’m really disappointed in your investigation. Because when I went to your attorneys, I asked them explicitly if this was a waste of my time, because none of this happened at a Democratic Party event,” Chapin said.
Instead, the attorneys reassured Chapin the investigation could move forward, he said. In the end, a judicial commission decided they did not have jurisdiction because the alleged assault did not take place at a Democratic Party event — as Chapin feared.
“You knew that this was a sham,” Chapin said. “You should all be fucking ashamed of yourselves.”
The Democratic Party endorsement is a highly valued political rubber stamp and puts endorsed candidates’ faces on mailers sent throughout the city every election. It is particularly valued in lower-profile races.
As the congressional contest to replace Rep. Nancy Pelosi, the state billionaire tax, and the effort to save Muni and BART begin to soak up airwaves and cellphone ad space, that rubber stamp may prove decisive for the candidates running for District 8 supervisor, the contest for a district of roughly 85,000 people in the Castro, Noe Valley, and nearby neighborhoods.
As first revealed by The Standard in June, Chapin alleges that Yekutiel forcibly squeezed his testicles at a house party in 2020. After seeing Yekutiel launch his run for office earlier this year, Chapin filed a police report, saying he felt responsible for protecting others.
Prosecutors did not charge Yekutiel. An investigation by The Standard found that SFPD’s special victims unit is understaffed and has pursued fewer cases than it has in years.
“I’m grateful to have earned the San Francisco Democratic Party’s endorsement,” Yekutiel said, in a statement. Our campaign is focused on delivering results on the issues voters care about most, making San Francisco more affordable, building the housing we need, supporting small businesses, and keeping our neighborhoods safe.”
Early in the meeting, Tung, the party chair, told the board that the party’s independent process did not substantiate Chapin’s allegations, nor did it discount them.
“The jurisdiction of this body is limited in nature,” Tung said. “It’s up to you how you take this information and weigh it in your endorsement process.”
While Chapin’s accusation against Yekutiel kicked off the party meeting, most public comment came from District 8 residents supporting Yekutiel, including his campaign volunteers.
Chapin sat in the front row as dozens of people sang Yekutiel’s praises.
“What is the point of the money, time and energy the Democratic Party pumps out if you aren’t supporting candidates who will take a risk on big projects worthy of San Francisco and tens of thousands of members of District 8,” said Julia Isbester, a District 8 resident, at the meeting. “We should be supporting visionary generational talent, like Manny.”
At times, Chapin shouted critiques of those speaking, alleging they were supporting someone who had committed sexual assault. Tung repeatedly asked Chapin to respect public commenters, and at one point called a five-minute recess after asking Chapin to stop interrupting speakers.
Some public speakers spoke in favor of District 8 Board of Supervisors candidate Gary McCoy, including many representatives of labor, from unions representing City College of San Francisco teachers to regional bus drivers and more.
Apollo Wallace, a business agent with Teamsters Local 2785, told the party that the Teamsters gave McCoy its sole endorsement.
“As a third-generation San Franciscan, raised in District 8, I support Gary McCoy and I stand with survivors,” Wallace said.
summary: A raucous and, occasionally, ill-tempered meeting of the San Francisco Democratic Party Wednesday night featured impassioned pleas, angry interruptions and a five-minute recess as members weighed whether to endorse District 8 supervisor candidate Manny Yekutiel. Two months ago, a political organizer accused San Francisco supervisor candidate Manny Yekutiel of forcibly grabbing his testicles and attempting to penetrate him with his fingers at a 2020 house party.
